SNACS review rules (v2.6; from authorized examples)

Represent each target as [scene_role, lexical_function]; both labels use p. prefixes. Role is the relation in context; function is the lexical contribution of the adposition or marker. They can match or differ through construal.

Examples and distinctions:
- In ‘went to the school’, school affiliation is p.Org as role, p.Goal as function: destination wording construes the institution as a goal.
- In ‘Each of you’, of is p.QuantityItem/p.Whole (partitive quantity relation to a whole set). In ‘proud of your contributions’, of is p.Stimulus/p.Topic: the contributions evoke the emotion and are its topic.
- ‘Your contributions’ can be p.Agent/p.Gestalt when the possessor is the actor in the possessed noun’s event. Ordinary ‘your money’ is p.Possessor/p.Possessor.
- ‘Throughout the year’ expressing duration is p.Duration/p.Duration.
- ‘By saying’ when saying is the means of an act is p.Means/p.Means.
- ‘At Lovely Nails’ and ‘on Military Road’ locating an event/place are p.Locus/p.Locus.

Choose labels from the complement and governing predicate/construction, not the preposition alone. Distinguish partitive of (QuantityItem/Whole), stimulus/topic of emotional predicates, and possessive uses. For possessives, determine whether the possessor is an agent in the possessed noun’s event or simply a possessor. Use Locus for where an event or property holds; use Goal when a directional relation is expressed.
